chunks: A number of scholars narrated to me on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) that he said: Narrated to us my father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan and Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil, from Abdullah ibn Ja'far al-Himyari that he said: I asked Muhammad ibn Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him): Have you seen the Master of this Affair?

He said: Yes, and the last time I saw him was at the Sacred House of God, and he (peace be upon him) was saying: O Allah, fulfill for me what You promised. Muhammad ibn Uthman (may Allah be pleased with him) said: And I saw him, Divine bliss be for him, clinging to the curtains of the Kaaba at the Mustajaar (spout/corner) as he was saying: O Allah, avenge for me Your enemies.

key_terms.الْمُسْتَجَارُ: The spout or corner of the Kaaba
key_terms.بَيْتُ اللَّهِ الْحَرَامُ: The Sacred House of God (the Kaaba)
key_terms.صَاحِبُ هَذَا الْأَمْرِ: The Master of this Affair (referring to the Imam)

ai.seo_question: What did the Imam say when he was seen at the Kaaba during the Occultation?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* provides a key eyewitness account of Imam al-Hasan al-Askari (peace be upon him) during the Minor Occultation, specifically identifying Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amri as one of the Four Deputies. It captures the Imam’s dual supplication at the Kaaba for the realization of divine promise and vengeance against enemies, reflecting the Shia eschatological expectation of the Mahdi’s return to establish justice. This event underscores the continuity of the Imam’s presence and spiritual authority even while concealed from public view.
